why:
Substance survives all three checks; only the page citation is wrong.

**1. Quote — verbatim, but NOT on the cited page.** `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md` (465 lines) contains ZERO occurrences of "labeled", "labelled", "canonical", or "Stop Task". The sentence is verbatim on a DIFFERENT page: `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md:158` — "The label shown for a tool in the transcript and permission dialog can differ from its canonical name. For example, the tool labeled `Stop Task` in the transcript has the canonical name `TaskStop`. Permission rules and [hook matchers](/docs/en/hooks) match the canonical name only, so a rule written as `Stop Task` doesn't match. For deny and ask rules, the startup warning above catches the mismatch. Use the canonical names listed in the [tools reference](/docs/en/tools-reference)." Both `permissions` (line 139) and `tools-reference` (line 167) are rows in `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so the contract source is valid Claude Code corpus — this is a misattributed citation, not a fabricated quote, so it does not refute outright. (`tools-reference.md` does support the finding indirectly: line 9 — "The tool names are the exact strings you use in permission rules, subagent tool lists, and hook matchers" — and line 55 lists `TaskStop` in the tool table, with `Permission required: No`.) Our own repo already cites this correctly at `runtime-agent-definition.ts:93` ("permissions.md:158"), so the doc-sweep row's PAGE column contradicts the code comment it is describing.

**2. Cited file:lines — confirmed exactly.**
- `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts:262` is literally `binding('stop_task', 'stop_task', 'stopTask', 'stopTask'),`. The `binding` factory (`:219-236`) has `permissionName = handlerName` as its 5th default, so this yields descriptorId `stop_task`, piName `stop_task`, bindingName/handlerName/permissionName `stopTask`. The 5th arg is available and unused here.
- `:351-353` — `PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES = Object.freeze([...new Set(PI_TOOL_BINDINGS.flatMap(b => [b.permissionName, b.descriptorId]))].sort())`. Neither projection can produce `TaskStop`.
- `runtime-agent-definition.ts:94-95` — `taskstop: ['stopTask', 'stop_task'],` inside `PI_RUNTIME_AGENT_TOOL_ALIASES`, consumed only by `normalizePiRuntimeAgentToolName` (`:106-114`), i.e. subagent/skill tool lists. Confirmed.

**3. One layer up / one layer down — no upstream handler exists.**
- Up: all three production consumers pass the same list unmapped — `permissions-config.ts:529` (Claude `settings.json` import), `managed-policy.ts:1017` (managed tier), `pi-agent.ts:3032` (hook-updated session rules). No `normalizeToolName` / alias table sits on any of them (grep for `CLAUDE_TOOL_NAME|TOOL_NAME_ALIAS|canonicalToolName|normalizeToolName` over non-dist sources returns nothing).
- Down: BOTH matcher sites miss. The gate (`permission-dsl.ts:648`) compares a `kind:'tool'` rule against `request.semanticId` (`stop_task`) and `request.toolName` (permissionName = `stopTask`). The manifest-removal identity matcher (`:936-938`) is broader — semanticId, permissionName, bindingName, piName — and that set is `{stop_task, stopTask, stopTask, stop_task}`. `TaskStop` reaches neither, so both the "deny matches nothing" and the `claude_rule.unknown_tool` warning consequences hold.
- Not an owner decision: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3's nine entries are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, and listSessionSummaries. None is this.
- Not the deliberate product difference: `stopTask` is Pi's own upstream tool name (`pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts` → `createStopTaskTool`, `name: 'stopTask'`), not a NESSY_/rebrand rename, and nothing here touches subscription flows or the gateway.
- The repo's own dominant posture points the other way, which is what makes this a real inconsistency rather than a style choice: `harness-tool-descriptor.ts:303-309` states that "the handlerName — which is also the permissionName — must be the documented spelling verbatim. That alone makes an imported `EnterWorktree` permission rule match", and `Monitor`, `NotebookEdit`, `ReportFindings`, `SendUserFile`, `PushNotification`, `TaskCreate`… all follow it. `stopTask` is on the non-conforming side.
correctedState:
Two corrections the row needs before it is actionable.

(a) **PAGE is wrong.** The sentence lives at `permissions.md:158`, not `tools-reference.md`. `tools-reference.md` contributes only the supporting line 9 ("The tool names are the exact strings you use in permission rules, subagent tool lists, and hook matchers") and the `TaskStop` table row (Permission required: **No**). Re-file the row against `permissions`.

(b) **SUBSYSTEM must be named — this is the Pi harness only.** On the Claude SDK backend `TaskStop` is a live built-in: `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:136` lists `'TaskStop'` in `BUILT_IN_TOOLS`, and `packages/ui/src/components/chat/task-checklist.ts:21` handles `TaskStop` activities. The unmatched-rule consequence is confined to `PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES` and the Pi permission DSL. An unqualified "TaskStop is not a known tool" is too broad.

One nuance that bounds the severity, worth recording alongside: the repo already has a tested, reasoned posture for this exact shape at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/claude-permission-rules.test.ts:245-247` — "Nessy's find tool is `Find`; Claude's `Glob` names nothing here, and the rule really would match no tool, so the warning is the correct answer." `TaskStop`→`stopTask` is structurally identical to `Glob`→`Find`, so whoever fixes this should decide the general rule (adopt every documented Claude spelling as `permissionName`, per `harness-tool-descriptor.ts:303-309`) rather than patching one binding. If fixed, the seam is the unused 5th `binding()` argument: `binding('stop_task', 'stop_task', 'stopTask', 'stopTask', 'TaskStop')` — and note the adjacent `Monitor` comment (`:297-302`) warning that `permissionName` is also the transcript-facing label, so the same change is not free everywhere.
